newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Caltex cautious on company performance this year.
newsitem.headline: Caltex cautious on company performance this year.

text.p: Caltex Petroleum Corp chairman David J. Law-Smith said on Monday that if oil refining margins continued to be under pressure, the company's total performance this year will be "questionable".
Asked in an interview whether the company's performance would be better than last year, Law-Smith told Reuters; "The total performance, if refining margins continue, that will be questionable."
Caltex is a joint venture of major U.S. oil companies Texaco Inc and Chevron Corp. In 1995, Caltex companies generated sales of about $15 billion.
"If one is to say that refining margins are to be under pressure for the rest of the year, the whole of this area would have a level that is less than would be expected," he said.
He said other oil companies and analysts had also discussed the impact of weak refining margins on the performance of oil companies.
However, he said Caltex's refining margins to date "averaged what we anticipated".

"What I can say is that we have a significant contribution to both shareholder companies on our goals and to make absolutely certain that under any marketing conditions, we provide competitive returns to their shareholders," he said.
To face the weak margins, especially during summer months, Caltex maintains lower output at its refineries to "accomodate the volatility in refining margins," he said.
Law-Smith said Asia was generally short of oil products "but that shortfall is closing" with additional capacities coming onstream from new refineries and existing ones being upgraded.

"The dynamic that has changed is the globalisation of supplies to the extent that the shortfall in the Asian markets is being provided for by other markets in Europe and North America when it proved to be economically attractive," he said.
"When one is asked to give an opinion on refining margins, it now means a very thorough guess of worldwide supply and demand strategies of marginal refineries in Europe and North America."
He said while the supply side was better known, less known was the demand potential from countries like India, China, Indonesia and Vietnam as their economies mature and slow down.
"But I must admit that in the many years gone by, Caltex has underestimated the growth of consumption in the whole of Asia."
